name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Microwave Area Denial MAD-3 'Sunburn'
description: A tripod-mounted directed microwave emitter designed for area denial and crowd control. The MAD-3 projects a focused beam of millimeter-wave radiation that penetrates clothing and heats the water molecules in the top 1/64th of an inch of skin, creating an intensely painful burning sensation without causing visible injury at standard power settings. At elevated power levels — accessible through a field override that Arcturus officially states does not exist — the beam can cause second-degree burns, ignite flammable materials, and cook electronics. The weapon's psychological effectiveness relies on the invisible, inescapable nature of the pain — targets cannot see what is hurting them and cannot shield themselves with conventional cover.
legality: Licensed — military and authorized security installations
specifications:
beam type: 95 GHz millimeter wave
effective range: 20-200 meters
beam width: 2 meter diameter at 100 meters
power output: 100kW standard, field override to 250kW
weight: 85 kg on tripod
power source: Vehicle power feed or dedicated generator
time to pain threshold: 2 seconds at standard power
story_hooks: A MAD-3 at elevated power was used to cook the electronics in an entire server farm through the building's walls — the data destruction was total and untraceable to any conventional weapon.
Reports of invisible burning pain in a residential area have been dismissed as mass hysteria — but someone has set up a concealed MAD-3 and is slowly making an entire block uninhabitable.
related_entities: Crucible Industries Ceramic Stiletto CS-4 'Phantom Needle'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist apparatus of focused menace — a squat, angular emitter assembly mounted on a heavy tripod base. The dish-like transmitter array dominates, ringed with cooling vanes. Industrial and deliberate, suggesting capability rather than elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: Emitter assembly: 60cm wide × 45cm tall × 35cm deep. Tripod legs span 120cm. Total height mounted: 140cm. Barrel projection (emitter face): 20cm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and grounded — 85kg on tripod creates an impression of immobile authority. Requires two-person setup, deliberate positioning. Not a handheld weapon; it roots itself.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed aluminum frame and emitter housing. Steel tripod base with reinforced joints. Composite thermal management shrouding around the active array.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with anodized aluminum panels. Functional, unmarked. Heat scorching visible around emitter vents — faint discoloration from radiant output bleed. No attempt at concealment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, charcoal black thermal venting shrouds, satin steel tripod legs. Accent: faint orange-copper oxide staining around heat dissipation vanes.
physical_description.grip_texture: Tripod legs: knurled steel adjustment points. Control interface: rubberized polymer keypads. Hard-mount points: textured composite for tool engagement.
distinctive_features: Concentric cooling rings surrounding the 20cm emitter dish
Thermal management vents arranged radially — evidence of extreme heat generation
Articulated azimuth and elevation servo mounts with graduated scale markings
Recessed control panel with minimal LCD readout and override access beneath security plate
Cable management conduits for vehicle power feed or generator umbilical
Faint heat stress patterns on aluminum — browning and micro-warping from sustained operation
No visible aiming sight — targeting is electronic and invisible
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo stamped into upper mounting plate. Serial identifier engraved on control panel housing. Regulatory compliance plates buried beneath classified specifications seal. No model designation visible — only internal documentation references 'MAD-3.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Cooling vanes show dust accumulation and thermal stress. Tripod joints show micro-corrosion from GLMZ humidity. Control panel scuffed from gloved operation. Never pristine — always operational.
